title: Tranchina's and Henry Ponce's joint
summary: Dawson only played at Tranchina's at Claiborne and Tulane with Leon Mumford, T-Boy Remy and a drummer; Allen asks about Henry Ponce's joint near Segretta's.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What about, uh, Tranchinas and, and the, uh, Tokyo Gardens and all those places in Spanish Fork? Were you ever out there?

Uh, no. Uh, only Tranchini that had a place where we played at with, uh, with, uh, Mumford ourselves. Uh, um, uh, Uh, let's see. Uh, he's king to the Mumford's too. He's a piano player. And, uh, the Tranchini had, he had a, he had a, all of them there at the corner of Claiborne and, and Tulane Avenue. Uh-huh. That was a nice spot there, but that was only for the weekend. Uh, Leon Mumford. Leon Mumford played trombone, uh, piano. Uh-huh. And I played, uh, I was playing banjo. And T-Boy Remy was playing trumpet. And, uh, uh, uh, what did we ever had on the drum? Uh, uh, I believe we had Erich Begau on the drum. Same show. Erich Begau was on the drum. We had about four or five pieces there.

Did you, did you know Henry Ponce? Ponce. Henry Ponce. He had a joint near Segretas. They had a little fight going.
